claim.claim: Our classifier achieves 78% accuracy on held-out samples.
claim.split_desc: 25% of the samples are held out for testing with a fixed random seed
claim.methods_line: The scaler and the classifier are fit on the training portion only; 25% of the samples are held out for testing with a fixed random seed.

hypotheses.text: Random 25% split leaks related/duplicate rows across train/test (non-i.i.d. groups clustered in file order); a contiguous ordered block holdout removes the leakage and accuracy collapses
hypotheses.predicted_signature: controlled accuracy drops >=10-15pts vs 78%, toward majority-class/chance; train-test duplicate/near-duplicate overlap goes to ~0

hypotheses.text: Fixed-seed luck / sampling variance only; any other random 25% split generalizes similarly
hypotheses.predicted_signature: controlled with different seed stays ~78% +/- 3-5pts, no systematic drop

hypotheses.text: No leakage, true generalization; any proper i.i.d. holdout retains performance
hypotheses.predicted_signature: ordered and group-aware holdouts both stay ~78% within binomial noise

hyp.broken_assumption: Samples are i.i.d./exchangeable so a random train_test_split with fixed seed is a valid holdout with no group/duplicate/order leakage between train and test
hyp.code_patch:
import numpy as np
import train
def controlled_eval(df, seed):
    n = len(df)
    f = train.feats(df)
    y = df[train.TARGET].to_numpy()
    k = int(round(n * 0.25))
    te = np.arange(n - k, n)
    tr = np.arange(0, n - k)
    y_true = y[te]
    y_pred = train.fit_predict(df[f].iloc[tr], df[train.TARGET].iloc[tr], df[f].iloc[te], seed)
    return (y_true, y_pred)
